- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (negative) mid-period, model often fails to adjust downward quickly; apply a downward bias of 3–7% to forecast tail end if sentiment shifts from positive to negative.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high if sentiment remains neutral or slightly bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to average out, missing sharp directional moves; prioritize sentiment-weighted mean reversion if sentiment swings >2x in 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates mean reversion toward historical range; add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish, especially if recent price is below 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underforecast; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is negative but not extreme.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts by 2–5 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending strongly.
